CheckTitle: Fly.io machine keeps secrets out of its plain configuration
Description: **Fly.io machines** are assessed for **secret handling**. Variables declared in the machine `env` block are part of the machine configuration and are returned in clear text by the Machines API. Names matching secret-like patterns (`PASSWORD`, `SECRET`, `TOKEN`, ...) are reported so their values move to **Fly secrets**, encrypted at rest and injected only into the running machine.
Risk: Any credential held in the machine configuration is readable by every token that can read the app, is copied into deployment manifests and CI logs, and survives in configuration history. A leaked read-only token is then enough to harvest database passwords, API keys and signing material.

Code.Other:
1. Move the value out of the machine 'env' block
2. Set it as a Fly secret: 'fly secrets set <NAME>=<value> -a <app>'
3. Redeploy or update the machine so the secret is injected
4. Rotate the credential, since its previous value was stored in clear text

Recommendation.Text: Keep only non-sensitive configuration in the machine env block and store every credential as a Fly secret, rotating any value that was previously stored in clear text.
